sections.title: Sounds of or
paragraphs: The letters or usually sound like the vowel in (fork) /fɔːrk/. A vowel is a sound made with open air and no touch in the mouth. This letter pair has three different sounds in English words.

sections.title: Mouth shape
paragraphs: For the first sound, round your lips and pull your tongue back. Then curl your tongue tip back slightly. For the second sound, relax your lips and tongue in the middle of your mouth. For the third sound, keep your mouth half open and curl your tongue back gently. Touch your throat to feel your voice shake for all three sounds.

sections.title: Spelling patterns
paragraphs: In a stressed syllable, say the first sound, as in (corn) /kɔːrn/. A stressed syllable is a beat that you say with more strength. In an unstressed syllable, say the weak second sound, as in (doctor) /dɑːk.tər/. When these letters follow the letter w, say the third sound, as in (word) /wɜːrd/.

sections.title: Common errors
paragraphs: Do not roll your tongue when you say these sounds. Make sure you do not say the vowel in (word) /wɜːrd/ like the vowel in (corn) /kɔːrn/. After the letter w, keep your tongue relaxed in the centre of your mouth.
